S1.why: Label under the five tiles; the bracket already says 'these', so the number and 'gratis' are enough.

S2.why: Imperative of 'blijven bewaren': an invitation to carry on, with no limit word; the app already uses 'Limiet bereikt' for a warning, so that word stays out.

S3.s: Je hebt alle %lld gratis Cutlings gebruikt. Die blijven gratis en werken gewoon door.
S3.back: You have all 5 free Cutlings used. Those stay free and work just on.
S3.why: Informal 'je' as in the vocabulary; 'gewoon door' is how a Dutch speaker says nothing changes for them, and 'Cutlings' is the list's own word.

S4.why: Stated as a fact about their own first items, which a Dutch reader hears as generous; no 'Je kunt' sentence explaining a control.

S5.s: Je hebt %lld van je %lld gratis Cutlings gebruikt.
S5.back: You have 3 of your 5 free Cutlings used.
S5.why: Same number order as the brief, so plain %lld twice; reads correctly for 1 used as well, because the plural follows the total.

S6.why: 'Plek' is the everyday word for room; 'Ruimte voor' runs over the budget at 26 with the number.

S7.s: Je kunt tot %@ teksten en %lld afbeeldingen bewaren.
S7.back: You can up to 5.000 texts and 500 images save.
S7.why: The kinds named with the vocabulary's Tekst and Afbeeldingen in the plural, verb at the end as Dutch puts it.

S8.why: Dutch lists three with commas and 'en', no serial comma.

S9.s: Eén aankoop geldt voor alle drie, via je Apple Account.
S9.back: One purchase counts for all three, via your Apple Account.
S9.why: 'Geldt voor' is how Dutch says a purchase covers something; 'Apple Account' and 'je' as the vocabulary writes them.

S10.why: Infinitive headline, the usual form for a Dutch feature line; says once without the shop word 'eenmalig', which the button carries.

S11.s: Geen abonnement, geen advertenties, geen account nodig.
S11.back: No subscription, no advertisements, no account needed.
S11.why: The three absences the brief names, in the repeated 'geen' a Dutch speaker uses for exactly this list.

S12.why: The wording Dutch iOS apps use for the StoreKit restore action, imperative like the vocabulary's 'Ga door'.

S13.why: Bare infinitive plus the ellipsis character, the Dutch iOS form for a running action.

S14.why: 'voor eenmalig' before a price is the native Dutch shop phrase for a one-off payment; 25 characters plus the price.

S15.why: The same verb as S14 without the price, so the button does not change meaning when the price arrives.

S16.why: Apple's own Dutch for putting a prompt off; it postpones and does not refuse.

S17.why: The imperative Dutch iOS and macOS use on close buttons.

S18.why: 'Helemaal van jou' is warm and a little proud, and covers everything at once, the room included; stressed 'jou' because it ends the line.

S19.s: Bedankt. Zo steun je Cutling en de maker, die het in z'n eentje bouwt.
S19.back: Thanks. So support you Cutling and the maker, who it in his own builds.
S19.why: 'In z'n eentje' is the everyday way to say one person does it all alone; 'Bedankt' alone is clear right after the purchase and keeps it to two lines.

S20.s: Welkom terug. Je eerdere aankoop is hersteld.
S20.back: Welcome back. Your earlier purchase is restored.
S20.why: 'Hersteld' echoes the S12 link they just tapped, so the person sees their action worked.

S21.why: Spoken label, so the short participle form VoiceOver reads cleanly; no sentence needed.

S22.s: Nu plek voor %2$@ Cutlings. Je hebt er %1$lld.
S22.back: Now room for 5.000 Cutlings. You have there 21.
S22.why: Positional forms because the room comes first in Dutch; the pronoun 'er' carries the count, so it reads right for 1, 2, 5 and 21 with no plural on the count.

S23.s: Cutling is ontgrendeld. Plek voor %@ Cutlings.
S23.back: Cutling is unlocked. Room for 5.000 Cutlings.
S23.why: Announcement in two short spoken parts; 'Plek voor' repeats S6 so the room has one name.

S24.why: 'Niet gelukt' is the calm Dutch phrase with no fault in it; 'mislukt' sounds harder.

S25.s: De App Store is nu niet bereikbaar. Probeer het straks opnieuw.
S25.back: The App Store is now not reachable. Try it shortly again.
S25.why: 'Straks' is the Dutch word for in a little while; 'Probeer het opnieuw' is the standard Dutch iOS retry line.

S26.s: De App Store heeft deze aankoop niet bevestigd.
S26.back: The App Store has this purchase not confirmed.
S26.why: A plain statement of what the store did, so the person is not blamed.

S27.s: Er staat geen eerdere aankoop van Cutling op het Apple Account van dit apparaat.
S27.back: There stands no earlier purchase of Cutling on the Apple Account of this device.
S27.why: 'Er staat geen ... op' is how Dutch says a record holds nothing; names the account on this device, as the brief asks.

S28.s: De gratis versie bewaart %lld Cutlings. Ontgrendel Cutling eenmalig en bewaar er zoveel als je wilt.
S28.back: The free version keeps 5 Cutlings. Unlock Cutling once and keep of-them as many as you want.
S28.why: Two plain sentences Siri can speak; 'eenmalig' matches the button, 'er' refers back to Cutlings, 'je wilt' is the standard form.

S29.why: Sits under the 'Cutlings' title, so the noun is already on screen; 14 characters.

K1.why: Headline Dutch drops 'zijn'; 'op' means used up. The verb after the dot is the action the tap takes; 'Tik om te ontgrendelen' alone is 22 characters and would not fit 38.

M1.why: Imperative, the form Dutch macOS uses for command names such as 'Sluit venster'.

M2.why: M1 as a button, with the ellipsis character because it opens a window.

M3.why: Row label as a noun phrase, the list's own word.

M4.why: Dutch reads a used-of-total pair as 'van'; 7 characters.

M5.why: The row sits in the Cutling section, so the participle alone is the status, as Dutch Mac settings show states.

M6.s: Met één aankoop ontgrendel je Cutling op iPhone, iPad en Mac.
M6.back: With one purchase unlock you Cutling on iPhone, iPad and Mac.
M6.why: Verb-second after 'Met één aankoop', the natural Dutch order; devices listed as in S8.

M7.s: Ontgrendeld op iPhone, iPad en Mac met dit Apple Account.
M7.back: Unlocked on iPhone, iPad and Mac with this Apple Account.
M7.why: Participle fragment as a status line, as Mac settings captions read; 'Apple Account' as the vocabulary writes it.

M8.s: Je kocht Cutling al voordat het gratis werd, dus het blijft ontgrendeld. Bedankt daarvoor.
M8.back: You bought Cutling already before it free became, so it stays unlocked. Thanks for-that.
M8.why: 'Al' marks they were early; 'Bedankt daarvoor' thanks them for that purchase specifically, not in general.
